summary.text: The Kogi State capital, at the confluence of the Niger and Benue, and one of the most mixed towns in Nigeria.

peoples.name: Igala
peoples.note: Indigenous Igala fishermen lived at the confluence when the Attah ceded the land in 1841 (owner testimony). Igala is used at home and work across the town. No published figures give the share; the owner reports a large population.

languageUse.text: Strongly multilingual: an average resident speaks between four and nine languages. English and Pidgin are used between people of different groups.

history.text: At the meeting of the Niger and Benue. The Attah of Igala’s agents ceded land here to the British in 1841, and in 1857 William Balfour Baikie set up a trading post on the Niger bank. The colonial government listed it as a township in 1917; it is now the Kogi State capital.

livelihoods.text: Trade and commerce, thanks to its position at the confluence; the Oworo name Ilu Oke Oja means “the market town on the hill”. Farming and hunting around Agbaja hill.
